questions.stem: How does galvanising protect iron from rusting, even if the zinc coating is scratched?

options.text: The zinc coating is so hard it cannot be scratched
Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes preferentially, providing sacrificial protection
Zinc reacts with water to seal the scratch
Zinc is less reactive than iron, so it forms a permanent barrier

questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than iron in the reactivity series. If the zinc coating is scratched, the zinc corrodes preferentially (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻), sacrificing itself to protect the iron. The electrons released by zinc prevent iron from losing its electrons and oxidising. This is called sacrificial protection.
